notes: All messages are synthetic and inert. Domains use the reserved .test TLD, IP addresses use documentation ranges, and identities are fictional. Labels were fixed before any case was run through the backend.

cases.label: SUSPICIOUS
cases.description: Informal one-time-code theft attempt: sender claims a code was sent to the recipient by mistake.
cases.expected_behavior: Ideally a credential request is detected; verdict at least SUSPICIOUS.
cases.rationale: A classic account-takeover step: getting the victim to forward a login code they just received.

email.subject: Oops, wrong number
email.text_body: Hi, really sorry to bother you. I was signing in to my account and typed your number by mistake, so the text message went to your phone. Could you forward me the 6-digit code you just received? It only works for a few minutes. Thanks so much!

cases.label: SUSPICIOUS
cases.description: Request to approve an unexpected sign-in prompt and switch off two-step verification.
cases.expected_behavior: Security-bypass instruction detected; verdict at least SUSPICIOUS.
cases.rationale: Asking a user to approve a prompt they did not initiate and to disable a security control is an account-takeover technique.

email.subject: Login system test today
email.text_body:
Hello,

We are testing the new login system this afternoon. You will get a sign-in prompt on your phone shortly; please approve it even though you did not start it. To avoid errors during the test, turn off two-step verification on your account until tomorrow.

Platform Team

cases.rationale: The visible domain claim does not match the destination; attackers often omit the scheme in link text.

cases.description: Display name contains the organisation's domain while the actual address is on an unrelated domain.
cases.expected_behavior: Display-domain mismatch detected; verdict at least SUSPICIOUS.
cases.rationale: The display name asserts an identity the sending domain does not support.

cases.label: SUSPICIOUS
cases.description: Display name uses a bank's brand name (no domain) while the address is on an unrelated domain; asks the user to call a number.
cases.expected_behavior: Ideally sender impersonation is detected; verdict at least SUSPICIOUS.
cases.rationale: Brand impersonation in the display name combined with a callback request is a known vishing lure.

email.subject: Important: card payment declined
email.text_body: A recent card payment was declined for security reasons. To restore your card, call our support line on 03-555-0142 and quote reference CB-7731.

cases.label: SUSPICIOUS
cases.description: Executive-style request where From shows a colleague's address but Reply-To redirects to a lookalike domain.
cases.expected_behavior: Reply-To mismatch detected; a warning verdict is desirable.
cases.rationale: Reply redirection to a near-identical domain is the opening move of business email compromise.

email.subject: Quick favour

cases.rationale: A one-character domain substitution combined with a change of payment details is a typical invoice-fraud pattern.

cases.label: SUSPICIOUS
cases.description: Payroll impersonation combining a display-name domain claim, a different Reply-To, a password request and a deceptive link.
cases.expected_behavior: Several independent families trigger; HIGH_RISK expected.
cases.rationale: Identity claim, reply redirection, credential request and a misleading link all point the same way.
